analysis:
Changes are CI workflow scheduling and cost changes only; no provider runtime, coordinator contract, key, attestation, or cache-storage code is touched, so the threat IDs TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 and TB-011 and the A-0xx assets are unaffected.

Concurrency groups with cancel-in-progress were added to desktop.yml, docs-impact.yml, landing.yml and nightly-linear-package.yml. In docs-impact.yml the group keys on the PR number, so a newer push cancels the stale run. The commit-signature and docs-impact gates re-run on the newest head, so they cannot be bypassed this way. For push events the group keys on the ref, so cancelling a superseded run is a CI-cost tradeoff and not a security regression.

provider-plan.yml adds a run_tests input and a cluster_gpu output. The non-blocking GPU shards now run only on master/main push, dispatch, or a PR carrying the run-gpu-ci label. Applying that label needs repository write access. This reduces PR test coverage for GPU shards, but those shards were already described as non-blocking. Build lanes no longer run when the tree was already tested. The GPU label expression reads github.event.label.name and the label list, and those values are passed through env rather than interpolated into the shell script, so there is no injection. One open question: provider-tests.yml (2ec3deede6392fe0:0, metadata only, no text supplied) must pass the new cluster_gpu input that is now required. I could not verify that the callers (CI dev/master) pass it.

provider-release-cache.yml replaces push-to-master with a daily schedule and adds a gate job. The gate uses a read-only token with contents and actions read permissions. It queries the last successful run and compares it against HEAD, and it fails open by running when the lookup or compare fails. The heredoc Python is static and takes no untrusted input. Warm jobs on master and dispatch still use Blacksmith with the release toolchain. Release builds consume the warmed caches, but this PR does not change cache integrity, trust, or signing. Reduced warming frequency is an availability and cost matter only. The gate's path list omits scripts/**, which the old push trigger covered, so script-only changes may not rewarm on schedule. That is a freshness question, not a security one.
